messages:
marta: Quick note - nightly 4xA100 inference with new kernel-selection routing shows a p50 latency increase ~12% after turning on 'proto:auto'. tagging @jong @kai for visibility.

jong: Can you share which workload? short vs long seq, and batch sizes?

marta: Short sequences (seq_len=128), batch=4, KV cache warm. Baseline was manual proto=LL and channels=4; new router runs proto:auto, channels:auto. Summary numbers I saw: 
```
baseline p50: 41.9ms
auto p50:     47.0ms
throughput: ~-9%
GPU util: slight increase in NCCL wait time
```

kai: We didn't change kernel vectorization or int8 paths, right? That can affect small sequences.

marta: Correct - kernel selection code untouched. Only change was letting NCCL pick proto/algo via proto:auto. My hypothesis: when proto flips to LL128 it interacts poorly with our channel mapping for these tiny collective sizes.

ryan: Can you reproduce with nccl-tests? Try forcing combinations: proto in [LL, LL128], channels in [1,2,4,8], algo choices. Example command: 
```
./build/all_reduce_perf -b 4 -e 65536 -f 2 --ngpus 4 --algo ring --proto LL128 --channels 2
```

marta: I ran a quick micro-sweep. Condensed p50 from a single-run set: 
```
channels=1 proto=LL    p50 40.7ms
channels=2 proto=LL    p50 41.6ms
channels=4 proto=LL128 p50 45.8ms
channels=8 proto=LL128 p50 47.1ms
channels=4 proto=LL    p50 41.9ms
```
So when proto switches to LL128 with same channel count perf regresses.

jong: That aligns with a theory: LL128 aggregates packets differently; for our variable small-message stream (KV traffic + short tokens) it can increase serialization. Also channel->peer mapping across NVLink islands matters.

kai: Do we assign channels topology-aware? If channels get round-robin mapped across NVLink islands, that could increase cross-island traffic and hurt overlap.

marta: Router's channel assignment is currently round-robin by peer index. Autoscaling tries to increase throughput but isn't NVLink-topology aware.

ryan: Any visibility in timelines? Are kernels taking longer or just queued?

marta: I uploaded an NSight capture and asked perf infra to summarize. infra-bot posted: perf job 1789602501 summary: NCCL ops show extra enqueued wait time between GPU kernels in the decode loop; NCCL kernel durations stable, but pre-launch wait increased ~8-12ms. SM occupancy unchanged. Host CPU not saturated. Seems like host-side enqueue/scheduling behavior changed with proto choices.

kai: Kernels themselves are fine then. So it's scheduling/serialization inside NCCL under our mapping. Two approaches: (A) force proto=LL for small sequences, (B) make channel mapping topology-aware so channels stay within NVLink islands.

jong: Also test forcing algo=ring vs algo=tree; NCCL 'auto' sometimes picks tree for certain peer counts which can harm our latency for small messages. Let's run a matrix: proto=[LL,LL128], algo=[ring,tree,auto], channels=[1,2,4,8], mapping=[rr,per-island].

marta: I'll run that matrix overnight and push the per-config CSV to /perf/matrix/. Will also add traces around kv_cache.prefetch and router.enqueue to see if we produce more frequent small all-reduces under auto.

ryan: Good. Also note earlier I saw that forcing LL128 with channels=1 returned near-baseline numbers. So interaction is not monotonic; channel parallelism changes packetization behavior under LL128.

kai: That suggests LL128 may create larger aggregated payloads per channel; with many channels each channel has smaller slices and overhead multiplies. Per-island mapping could reduce cross-island serialization.

jong: Plan: (1) run full matrix and upload results, (2) implement an opt-in per-island channel mapping toggle in router, (3) add lightweight KV-prefetch traces and enqueue timing for correlating stalls, (4) gate proto:auto behind rollout flag and keep safe default (proto=LL) until we have stable numbers. Agree?

marta: Agree. I'll kick off runs and post a compact CSV and the NSight captures here once done. Assigning canary rollout flag to @kai for approval once we have a new default.

perf-bot: CI: nightly inference-microbench (4xA100) - triggered matrix run 1789602530; results will land in /perf/matrix/1789602530.csv
